bug_categories.description: Swap or mis-assign input bits when slicing datain into ai..ji, e.g. ii = datain[6] and fi = datain[5], or hi/ji swapped.
bug_categories.applicability: The 10-bit datain is decomposed into named wires (ai,bi,ci,di,ei,ii,fi,gi,hi,ji). The 8b/10b ordering has 'ii' between 'ei' and 'fi', so a swapped index silently corrupts the 6b/4b sub-block decoding and the output data.

bug_categories.description: Reorder fields in the dataout concatenation, e.g. { ho, ko, go, fo, eo, do_, co, bo, ao } or swap eo and do_, so the decoded byte and K flag land in wrong bit positions.
bug_categories.applicability: dataout = { ko, ho, go, fo, eo, do_, co, bo, ao } packs a 9-bit output (K flag as MSB). Swapping any adjacent fields keeps the width valid but misplaces data/control bits.

bug_categories.description: Replace AND with OR or drop a negation in the symbol-class helper terms, e.g. p31 = !aeqb & ci & di & !ceqd & ai & bi, or p13 using ci|di instead of !ci & !di.
bug_categories.applicability: The p22/p13/p31/p40/p04 population-count classifiers (derived from aeqb/ceqd) feed every downstream signal: disp6a, compa..compe, code_err, and disp_err. A single wrong operator causes widespread decode and disparity errors.

bug_categories.bug_type: Decode correction term (comp*) omission or swap
bug_categories.description: Remove one product term from compa..compe or swap terms between them, e.g. use p22aceeqi in compa or drop cndnenin from compc, so specific 5b/6b codewords decode to wrong values.
bug_categories.applicability: ao..eo = input ^ comp*, and each comp* is a large OR of specific code patterns (p22bceeqi, p31i, p13dei, abei, anbnenin, ...). The XOR correction is only wrong for the specific codewords whose term was altered, making the bug subtle.

bug_categories.description: Alter the running-disparity computation, e.g. dispout = (fghjp31 | disp6b & fghj22 | hi & ji) | (hi | ji) or disp6b using dispin inverted, or disp6a2 = p31 | dispin.
bug_categories.applicability: dispout depends on disp6b, which is built from disp6a/disp6a2/disp6a0 and dispin, combined with the 4b classifiers fghjp31/fghj22. An error corrupts the disparity passed to the next symbol while leaving the data output mostly correct.

bug_categories.description: Change ko, k28 or k28p conditions, e.g. make k28p = (ci | di | ei | ii) or drop a term of ko such as the p13 & !ei & ii & gi & hi & ji case, causing incorrect K flag and affecting fo/go/ho.
bug_categories.applicability: ko, k28, and k28p drive the K output bit and the fo/go/ho 4b decode (k28p toggles between the fo/go formulas). Errors misclassify K28.x and K23/27/29/30.7 symbols and the data decode of the 4b sub-block.

bug_categories.description: Delete, negate or change a term in the long OR chains, e.g. remove 'p40 | p04', change 'disp6p & disp4p' to 'disp6p | disp4p', or flip dispin polarity in a disp_err term such as '!dispin & !disp6p & !fi & !gi'.
bug_categories.applicability: code_err and disp_err are large OR-of-products with many corner cases for invalid 10b codes and disparity violations. Altering a term yields missed or false error detection for particular illegal codewords without affecting data outputs.

bug_categories.description: Swap the disp6p/disp6n or disp4p/disp4n definitions, e.g. disp4p = fghjp13 and disp4n = fghjp31, or interchange the ei&ii conditions in disp6p/disp6n.
bug_categories.applicability: disp6p/disp6n/disp4p/disp4n are used in both code_err and disp_err. Swapping polarity leaves the structure valid but flips which combinations are flagged as disparity violations, and can cause legal symbols to be flagged and illegal ones to pass.
